name: SVD Decomposition Analysis
description: Applies Singular Value Decomposition to detect rank-deficiency patterns typical of AI-generated images, based on eigenvalue distribution anomalies.
mechanism:
This method applies Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) analysis for forensic image authentication:

1. **Block-wise SVD Computation**: The image is partitioned into blocks, and for each block matrix A ∈ ℝᵐˣⁿ, the SVD A = UΣVᵀ is computed. The singular values σ₁ ≥ σ₂ ≥ ... ≥ σᵣ capture the energy distribution across orthogonal rank-1 components following Eckart & Young (1936).

2. **Singular Value Spectrum Analysis**: The decay profile of singular values is analyzed. Natural image blocks exhibit characteristic decay patterns — smooth regions decay rapidly (low effective rank), while textured regions show gradual decay. AI-generated images often produce anomalous decay profiles with unexpected rank distributions.

3. **Effective Rank Mapping**: The effective rank ρ(A) = exp(H(σ̃)), where H is the Shannon entropy of normalized singular values σ̃ᵢ = σᵢ/Σσⱼ, provides a continuous measure of block complexity. A spatial map of effective rank reveals regions with unnatural complexity — either over-smoothed (low rank) or artificially textured.

4. **Principal Component Residual Analysis**: After retaining the top-k singular components (capturing structural content), the residual R = A − UₖΣₖVₖᵀ contains noise, texture detail, and potential artifacts. The statistical properties of this residual differ systematically between natural photographs (sensor noise characteristics) and AI-generated images.

5. **Forensic Scoring**: The spatial distribution of SVD statistics (effective rank, spectral decay rate, residual statistics) is analyzed for consistency. Manipulated or AI-generated regions show characteristic SVD signatures — truncated singular value spectra, abnormal rank distributions, or residuals lacking genuine sensor noise characteristics.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
